correctness.rationale: The fixed normalized gcd gives coprime increasing a_n<b_n for every k≥2. For coprime a<b, choose α inverse of a modulo b in [1,b−1] and β=(ab+1−aα)/b in [1,a]. The complementary Bézout identity gives either the witness ((α−1)/2,(β−1)/2) to M when both α,β are odd, or ((b−α−1)/2,(a−β−1)/2) to M−1 otherwise; the latter two numerators are odd by aα+bβ=ab+1 mod 2. Every target <ab has at most one nonnegative representation because x is determined mod b; Frobenius complement F=ab−a−b=2M−1 proves only one of M,M−1 is representable, with a=1 handled separately. Under (a,b)→(b,kb−a), transported (α,β)→(kα+β−a,b−α) satisfies the new Bézout equation and positivity. Modulo 2 this transformation permutes all six admissible parity states in three 2-cycles if k even, or two 3-cycles if k odd, each with nonconstant δ pattern and exact least period. Independent exact six-state calculation reproduced these cycles and least periods. Original verify.py was inspected; its finite tests cannot substitute for the parity-state proof.
residual_risks: Requires k≥2, positive A<B and invariant gcd normalization; no assertion for signed/nonmonotone recurrences.
The δ period does not mean the unbounded integer solution coordinates are periodic.
